discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, establishing moiré quantum matter

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University / Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and moiré superlattices
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene layers to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so that Coulomb interactions dominate. Jarillo-Herrero (Nature 2018) realised this with tear-and-stack fabrication. He found gate-tunable correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in one device, on a phase diagram strikingly like that of the cuprates. Twist angle became a new control knob for quantum matter. A single, clean, electrostatically tunable platform now hosts Mott and Wigner crystal states, orbital ferromagnetism, Chern insulators and, more recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall effects at zero field. Hundreds of groups worldwide, working in transport, optics and scanning probes, have entered this field of moiré quantum materials. It has changed what physicists can design and measure in strongly correlated, topological low-dimensional systems.
